group-anagrams.clue: Group strings that are equivalent after their characters are rearranged.
group-anagrams.baseline: For each word, compare it with every existing group representative; repeated character sorting can make this O(n²·k log k) time.
group-anagrams.bottleneck: The same anagram relationship is rediscovered for many pairs.
group-anagrams.optimal: Build a canonical key for each word, such as its 26-letter frequency tuple, and append the word to that key's group. The key represents the multiset of characters independent of order.
group-anagrams.complexity: O(n·k) time and O(n·k) extra space for lowercase English letters, counting grouped words and keys.
group-anagrams.edge: The statement restricts input to lowercase English letters; an alphabet-independent key can sort each word at O(k log k) cost.
group-anagrams.takeaway: Choose a canonical signature for the property that defines group membership.

subarray-sum-equals-k.clue: Count contiguous ranges whose sum equals a target, especially when values may be negative.
subarray-sum-equals-k.baseline: Choose every start index and extend the end while accumulating a running sum: O(n²) time and O(1) extra space.
subarray-sum-equals-k.bottleneck: Every candidate range recomputes a relationship between two prefix positions.
subarray-sum-equals-k.optimal: At running prefix sum s, count earlier prefixes equal to s-k. Store prefix-sum frequencies, beginning with prefix 0 occurring once; this counts all matching earlier boundaries, including duplicates.
subarray-sum-equals-k.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) extra space.
subarray-sum-equals-k.edge: Negative values prevent a simple sliding-window shrink rule; seed the frequency map with {0: 1} to count ranges starting at index 0.
subarray-sum-equals-k.takeaway: Turn a range sum into a difference between two prefix sums.

longest-repeating-character-replacement.clue: Find the longest substring that can become one repeated character after at most k edits.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.baseline: Check every substring while maintaining its letter counts and whether length minus the most common count is at most k: O(n²) time, O(1) extra space for the fixed alphabet.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.bottleneck: Each start position explores many overlapping windows.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.optimal: Slide a window and track its most frequent letter. If window length minus that count exceeds k, move the left boundary. The largest valid window seen is the answer.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space because the alphabet has 26 uppercase letters.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.edge: A nondecreasing historical maximum frequency is sufficient for this length-only result; the retained window may be temporarily stale but cannot inflate the maximum beyond a realizable earlier window.
longest-repeating-character-replacement.takeaway: A window is repairable when all non-majority characters fit within the edit budget.

daily-temperatures.clue: For each position, find the distance to its next strictly greater value.
daily-temperatures.baseline: Scan rightward from each day until finding a warmer temperature: O(n²) time and O(1) extra space besides the answer.
daily-temperatures.bottleneck: The same future temperatures are checked repeatedly for unresolved days.
daily-temperatures.optimal: Keep indices of unresolved days in a decreasing-temperature stack. A warmer current day resolves and removes every cooler stack top; store the index difference.
daily-temperatures.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space for the monotonic stack, plus the required output array.
daily-temperatures.edge: Pop only strictly cooler temperatures; equal readings are not warmer. Unresolved indices retain the answer's default zero.
daily-temperatures.takeaway: A monotonic stack keeps only unresolved candidates for the next greater element.

search-a-2d-matrix.clue: Search a row-wise sorted matrix whose rows continue one globally sorted sequence.
search-a-2d-matrix.baseline: Inspect each cell until the target is found: O(m·n) time and O(1) extra space.
search-a-2d-matrix.bottleneck: The row boundaries already establish a total order, but linear scan ignores it.
search-a-2d-matrix.optimal: Treat the matrix as a flattened sorted array. Binary-search a virtual index and map it to row = index // n and column = index % n.
search-a-2d-matrix.complexity: O(log(m·n)) time and O(1) extra space.
search-a-2d-matrix.edge: Use the number of columns for the virtual-index mapping and guard empty dimensions if the surrounding API permits them.
search-a-2d-matrix.takeaway: Exploit global order by searching virtual indices without allocating a flattened copy.

remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.clue: Remove a node by distance from the tail without needing random access.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.baseline: Count the list length, then walk again to the predecessor: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.bottleneck: A second traversal is needed because the target is measured from the end.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.optimal: Use a dummy node and two pointers separated by n links. Move both until the fast pointer reaches the tail, then bypass the target through the slow pointer.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.edge: The dummy predecessor handles removing the head when n equals the list length.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.takeaway: A fixed pointer gap converts distance-from-end into a single forward pass.

house-robber.clue: Choose non-adjacent values to maximize a sum along a line.
house-robber.baseline: Recursively branch on taking or skipping each house: O(2ⁿ) time and O(n) recursion depth.
house-robber.bottleneck: Many branches solve the same suffix subproblem.
house-robber.optimal: For each house, compare skipping it with taking it plus the best value two houses back. Keep only the previous two best totals.
house-robber.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
house-robber.edge: Initialize the rolling totals to zero so empty and one-house inputs work without special indexing errors.
house-robber.takeaway: When each choice blocks the adjacent choice, compare take-plus-two-back with skip.
